component.name: Apricot Studio
component.summary: Trim a clip from a video without re-encoding decisions

description.p: Apricot Studio does one thing: it takes a video, lets you mark a start and an end, and writes out that section. It is built for pulling a highlight out of a screen-recorder replay buffer without opening a full editor.

There are no export settings to answer. Every parameter is read from the file you opened — container, codec, resolution, frame rate, colour, GOP structure and bitrate — so the clip behaves like the recording it came from. Audio is stream-copied rather than re-encoded, so it takes no loss at all.

When the start of your selection lands on a keyframe, nothing needs to be decoded and the clip is copied straight out of the source: near-instant, and byte-for-byte identical. The app tells you which of the two paths an export will take before you run it.

ul.li: Frame-exact cuts at both ends
Instant, lossless export when the cut starts on a keyframe
Timeline with a filmstrip, audio waveform and keyframe markers
Quality presets that scale against the source, or a target file size
WebM and GIF export
Per-track audio selection for recordings with separate mic and desktop
Optionally move the original to the wastebasket after exporting
An interlaced video is recognised when it opens, and can be deinterlaced with BWDIF or QTGMC, each starting at its slowest profile
QTGMC is offered when VapourSynth with QTGMC is installed on the system
The filmstrip no longer decodes every keyframe in the file: it takes a fixed number of frames on a single core

description.p: No change to the app. The first release built entirely by CI: Windows ships as one zip, with ffmpeg and ffprobe beside the program.
Four things reported from real use: two repairs to the transport, one to the timeline, and a click that used to do nothing.

ul.li: The Pause button reads "Pause" again — its symbol was a character none of the bundled typefaces contained, so it drew as two empty boxes
Hold either one-frame button, beside the playhead or beside the In and Out timecodes, and it keeps stepping
The timeline's hover preview steps aside near the in and out handles, instead of covering the handle you are reaching for
Clicking the empty picture opens a video, the same as the Open button — it already said so, and already took a dropped file

description.p: Dropping a video onto the window now works on Wayland. It never had: the window toolkit implements drag-and-drop on X11, Windows and macOS and not on Wayland at all, so the app was reading a list that was always empty. It now speaks that part of the Wayland protocol itself.

ul.li: Drag-and-drop on Wayland, alongside the X11, Windows and macOS support that already worked
The picture says "Drop to open" while a file is held over the window
A dropped file that is not a video is named and refused, rather than silently ignored
The Cyberpunk theme's scanlines stop at the picture: over the interface they are texture, over your footage they were dirt

description.p: First release. Apricot Studio takes a video, lets you mark a start and an end, and writes out that section -- with no export settings to answer, because every parameter is read from the file you opened.

ul.li: Frame-exact cuts, and an instant bit-identical copy when the cut starts on a keyframe
Timeline with a filmstrip, audio waveform and keyframe markers
Quality presets that scale against the source, or a target file size
WebM and GIF export, and per-track audio for captures with separate mic and desktop
Two themes: Default, and Cyberpunk in crimson and teal with its own typeface
Optionally move the original to the wastebasket after exporting

description.p: This replaces the Python version of the same application. The ffmpeg commands behind every export are unchanged, argument for argument, and your theme, accent and recent files carry over the first time you run it.
